sentences.text: Ahmed Salman Rushdie , FRSL -LRB- -LSB- sælˈmɑːn_ˈrʊʃdi -RSB- अहमद सलमान रुशदी , ; born 19 June 1947 -RRB- is a British Indian novelist and essayist .	FRSL	Royal Society of Literature	British Indian	British Indian

His second novel , Midnight 's Children -LRB- 1981 -RRB- , won the Booker Prize in 1981 and was deemed to be `` the best novel of all winners '' on two separate occasions , marking the 25th and the 40th anniversary of the prize .	Booker Prize	Booker Prize	25th	Man Booker Prize#Winners	40th anniversary of the prize	The Best of the Booker
Much of his fiction is set on the Indian subcontinent .	Indian subcontinent	Indian subcontinent

He combines magical realism with historical fiction ; his work is concerned with the many connections , disruptions , and migrations between Eastern and Western civilizations .	magical realism	magical realism	historical fiction	Historical novel	Eastern	Eastern world

His epic fourth novel , The Satanic Verses -LRB- 1988 -RRB- , was the subject of a major controversy , provoking protests from Muslims in several countries .	The Satanic Verses	The Satanic Verses	a major controversy	The Satanic Verses controversy

Death threats were made against him , including a fatwā calling for his assassination issued by Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini , the Supreme Leader of Iran , on 14 February 1989 .	fatwā	fatwā	Ayatollah	Ayatollah	Ruhollah Khomeini	Ruhollah Khomeini	Supreme Leader of Iran	Supreme Leader of Iran
The British government put Rushdie under police protection .
In 1983 Rushdie was elected a fellow of the Royal Society of Literature , the UK 's senior literary organisation .	Royal Society of Literature	Royal Society of Literature
He was appointed Commandeur de l'Ordre des Arts et des Lettres of France in January 1999 .	Ordre des Arts et des Lettres	Ordre des Arts et des Lettres
In June 2007 , Queen Elizabeth II knighted him for his services to literature .	Queen Elizabeth II	Elizabeth II	knighted him	Knighthood of Salman Rushdie
In 2008 , The Times ranked him thirteenth on its list of the 50 greatest British writers since 1945 .	The Times	The Times
Since 2000 , Rushdie has lived in the United States .
He was named Distinguished Writer in Residence at the Arthur L. Carter Journalism Institute of New York University in 2015 .	New York University	New York University
Earlier , he taught at Emory University .	Emory University	Emory University
He was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Letters .	American Academy of Arts and Letters	American Academy of Arts and Letters
In 2012 , he published Joseph Anton : A Memoir , an account of his life in the wake of the controversy over The Satanic Verses .	The Satanic Verses	The Satanic Verses
Rushdie was strongly favoured to have received the Nobel Prize in Literature but the Nobel organisers were later quoted as saying that they would have been `` too predictable , too popular . ''
